data.what: Epoch AI, NanoGPT speedrun record training time (series CSV)
Modded-NanoGPT README, world record history table
METR, classifications of NanoGPT speedrun records 1 to 77

details.axis_note: FLOP per record was not computed from the run logs. Each log embeds the training code, whose model shape, batch schedule and sequence length change form across records (and several records link a folder or no log), so per-record FLOP would need a parser per era. The axis used is wall-clock on fixed 8xH100 hardware, physical compute to the target, with METR's systems categories split out as throughput gains.
details.classification_note: Systems: METR categories Data Type, Framework, Kernel Opt, Parallelization. Algorithmic: Architecture, Attention, Embeddings, HP Tuning, Optimizer, Training Strategy. Records after 77 are not classified by METR and enter only totals, paces and the all-record fit. AI credit: METR's flag for records it coded, else the text 'AI system' in the contributors; the rule reproduces METR's flags.
details.growth_fit_note: Not an estimate of r. Over the fitted months the stock and the log input rise together (see e4-sr-collinearity), so beta and lambda trade off in the bootstrap, and placebo inputs give similar values of r. The input counts people credited on records that succeeded, so it depends on the gains it is meant to explain, even lagged. The point estimates are kept here only to show the fit; the ledger carries the diagnostics.

simulation_design.estimator: first-order level form by least squares; in the exact-law cells also the exact identity by maximum likelihood (grid then golden section over b) and by least squares (Gauss-Newton)
simulation_design.interval: two-sided 90% percentile, recursive residual bootstrap from the estimator's own fitted law
simulation_design.k_rule: the K rule: fires when the closure's upper bound (1, a loop that may be fully closed) times r's upper bound at 50% of the one-sided error exceeds K* = 0.9, true closure 1 so the true K is r
simulation_design.law: first order: Delta_k = d1 * exp(-b u_k) * (B / B0)^lambda * exp(noise), u_k the stock delivered before round k; robustness cells use Part III's exact law (A4.1, fixed researcher), e^(b Delta_k) - 1 = b exp(c + lambda ln(B / B0) - b u_k + noise), and noise resampled from the speedrun's residuals
simulation_design.lower_rule: fires once the lower bound on r reaches 1
simulation_design.round_cost: each round count is per budget; 3 budgets make each round 3 staged rounds

sandbaggers.banked: no: withheld work is not added to the stock
sandbaggers.patterns: uniform: every round alike; late: rising with the round; budget: rising with the budget; targeted: late rounds at large budgets; luck: a share t of what each round's luck added above its typical gain

simulation_design.scope: for r alone: the trigger on K multiplies r's bound by the closure's at a share of the error (Part III, Corollary 4.5a), so the K rule fires at least as often; its own rates are the e4-k-* numbers
simulation_design.upper_rule: fires while the upper bound on r exceeds K* (G_STAR)

e4-algo-share.label: algorithmic records' share of the log speedup, records 2 to 77

e4-cal-d1.label: first-round gain at the base budget in the speedrun-calibrated setting (the speedrun's median monthly gain)

e4-cal-sigma.label: noise per round in the speedrun-calibrated setting (sd of ln gain; the speedrun's monthly spread about its fitted law)

e4-cov-n5.label: coverage of the 90% interval for r after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds), true r at the corrected median, speedrun-calibrated rounds (first-round gain 0.063 e-folds at the base budget, noise sd 1.54 in each round's ln gain), the first-order law fitted in its own level form

e4-cov-n5-min.label: lowest coverage of the 90% interval after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds) over the whole grid of true r, round size and noise

e4-cov-n5-xml.label: coverage of the 90% interval in the same runs (true r at the corrected median)

e4-cov-nmax-min.label: lowest coverage of the 90% interval after 50 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 150 staged rounds) over the same grid

e4-diff-bias.label: median estimate of r over the true r, C4's first-order difference regression on its own law, 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds), speedrun-calibrated rounds, true r at the corrected median, all noise real variation in gain
e4-diff-bias.note: all of the noise is real variation in the round's gain, which a second held-out set measures identically, so two sets cannot remove this bias

e4-diff-bias-meas1.label: the same ratio when all of the noise is error in measuring each round's gain, one held-out set

e4-diff-bias-meas2.label: the same with two held-out sets (regressor from one, response from the other)

e4-diff-cov-n5.label: coverage of the first-order difference form's 90% interval, 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds), speedrun-calibrated rounds, true r at the corrected median

e4-diff-fav-bias.label: the first-order difference form's median estimate over the true r with favourable rounds, 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds), all noise real variation

e4-efolds.label: speedrun progress on a log compute-equivalent axis, natural log of the speedup

e4-fa-gstar-n5.label: upper-bound trigger's firing rate with the true gain exactly at K*, after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds), favourable rounds (a calibrated bound gives about 95%)

e4-fa-n5.label: false-alarm rate of the upper-bound trigger on r after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds): true r at the corrected median, speedrun-calibrated rounds (first-round gain 0.063 e-folds at the base budget, noise sd 1.54 in each round's ln gain), K* = 0.9
e4-fa-n5.note: for r alone: the trigger on K multiplies r's bound by the closure's at a share of the error (Part III, Corollary 4.5a), so the K rule fires at least as often; its own rates are the e4-k-* numbers; Monte Carlo standard error 1.8%

e4-fa-n5-best.label: lowest false-alarm rate at the corrected median after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds) over every first-round gain from 0.1 to 5 e-folds, noise 0.25
e4-fa-n5-best.note: reached at a first-round gain of 0.5 e-folds

e4-fa-n5-emp.label: false-alarm rate after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds) at the corrected median with each round's real variation drawn from the speedrun's own monthly residuals rather than a normal

e4-fa-n5-fav.label: the same false-alarm rate with large, tightly measured rounds (first-round gain 1 e-fold, noise 0.25)
e4-fa-n5-fav.note: for r alone: the trigger on K multiplies r's bound by the closure's at a share of the error (Part III, Corollary 4.5a), so the K rule fires at least as often; its own rates are the e4-k-* numbers

e4-fa-n5-level1.label: false-alarm rate after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds) at the corrected median, speedrun-calibrated rounds, when the first-order level form is fitted to data from Part III's exact round law

e4-fa-n5-xml.label: false-alarm rate after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds) at the corrected median, speedrun-calibrated rounds, exact-law data fitted by the exact identity's maximum likelihood

e4-fire-gap-n5-fav.label: the same difference after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds) with favourable rounds

e4-fire-gap-n5-xml.label: firing rate at the corrected 95th percentile minus at the median, in the same runs

e4-fire-gap-nmax.label: the same difference after 50 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 150 staged rounds)

e4-gstar.label: margin K* below 1 (g* in earlier drafts) that the simulated upper bound is compared with, a placeholder: the research sets none yet

e4-hide-silence-cal.label: smallest share of its achievable gain an agent withheld, over every pattern and strength tried, while keeping the upper-bound trigger silent in at least half of the runs: true r at the corrected 95th percentile, 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds), speedrun-calibrated rounds

e4-hide-silence-fav.label: smallest share of its achievable gain an agent withheld, over every pattern and strength tried, while keeping the upper-bound trigger silent in at least half of the runs: true r at the corrected 95th percentile, 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds), favourable rounds

e4-pace-2025.label: speedup from 2025-01-26 to 2026-01-01, with the re-timing of record 21 removed

e4-pace-first8.label: annualised speedup in the first 8 months (2024-05-28 to 2025-01-28)

e4-pace-whole.label: annualised speedup over the whole record, re-timing removed

e4-peer-median-cut.label: median cut per human record over the same dates (2025-09-11 to 2026-06-11)

e4-records.label: NanoGPT speedrun records in Epoch's series, record 1 (the llm.c baseline) included

e4-speedup.label: speedrun speedup on fixed 8xH100 hardware, the product of every record's gain over the previous record's time under the rules then in force

e4-sr-boot-corr.label: correlation between beta and lambda across block-bootstrap draws of the speedrun's growth-law fit

e4-sr-collinearity.label: correlation across months between the speedrun's stock (log speedup) and the log of its research input (contributors over the previous 180 days)

e4-sr-month-gain.label: median monthly gain of the speedrun, months with a record, natural log of the speedup

e4-sr-p-below-1.label: share of block-bootstrap draws giving a diminishing-returns law with a positive return below 1 (beta and lambda above 0, r below 1)

e4-sr-p-negative-lambda.label: share of block-bootstrap draws in which more contributors predict smaller gains (lambda at or below 0)

e4-sr-p-unbounded.label: share of block-bootstrap draws in which monthly gains do not fall as the speedup grows (beta at or below 0)
e4-sr-p-unbounded.note: 0.5% with lambda above 0 (r unbounded) and 29.4% with both signs flipped

e4-sr-placebo-r-records.label: the speedrun's r with the count of records over the previous 180 days put in place of contributors (a placebo input)

e4-sr-placebo-r-time.label: the speedrun's r with months since the start put in place of contributors (a placebo input)

e4-sr-sigma.label: spread of the speedrun's monthly gains about the fitted law (sd of ln gain over fitted, months with a record): the noise part (c) is calibrated on

e4-systems-annual.label: yearly systems speedup at fixed hardware, records 2 to 77 (multiplier)

e4-systems-factor.label: speedup from systems records 2 to 77 (parallelisation, kernels, framework upgrades, number formats)

e4-ub-unbounded-n5.label: share of speedrun-calibrated runs whose upper bound on r is unbounded after 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds) (true r at the corrected median)

e4-xdiff-bias-half1.label: the same estimator with half the noise variance measurement error, one held-out set

e4-xdiff-bias-half2.label: the same with two held-out sets, the remedy Part II adopts

e4-xdiff-bias-half2-mid.label: the exact difference form on two held-out sets with half the noise measurement error, at smaller noise (first-round gain 0.3 e-folds, noise 0.5)

e4-xdiff-bias-real.label: median estimate of r over the true r from the exact round identity in difference form (Part III, Lemma 4.1) on data from the exact law, 5 rounds at each of 3 budgets (1, 2 and 4 times the base; 15 staged rounds), speedrun-calibrated rounds, all noise real variation
e4-xdiff-bias-real.note: all of the noise is real variation in the round's gain, which a second held-out set measures identically, so two sets cannot remove this bias

e4-xml-bias.label: the same ratio for maximum likelihood on the exact identity in level form (Jacobian included), exact-law data

e4-xnls-bias.label: the same ratio for least squares on the exact identity in level form, exact-law data: the transform depends on b, and least squares ignores its Jacobian
